s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging soft-tissue mass over the dorsum of the hand with a history of prior malignancy
salient_findings: 2-month history of a gradually enlarging mass
Soft-tissue mass over the second metacarpal dorsum with mild tenderness
Presence of Reed–Sternberg–like cells in an inflammatory background
key_facts: Diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma 6 years earlier
Mass located over the dorsum of the left hand
Mass measures approximately 4 cm in greatest dimension
Mild tenderness but no limitation of movement
Microscopic examination shows a mixture of inflammatory cells and myxoid stroma
Presence of epithelioid and spindle-shaped cells, lipoblast-like cells, and occasional Reed–Sternberg–like cells

shortlist.label: Acral myxoinflammatory fibroblastic sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: matches the location and histological features of the mass

shortlist.label: Myxoid liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with the myxoid stroma and lipoblast-like cells in the microscopic examination

shortlist.label: Myxofibrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: shares similar histological features with the presented case, including myxoid stroma and spindle-shaped cells

shortlist.label: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor

shortlist.label: Hodgkin lymphoma

raw.rationale: The presence of a mixture of inflammatory cells, myxoid stroma, epithelioid and spindle-shaped cells, lipoblast-like cells, and occasional Reed–Sternberg–like cells in a mass located over the dorsum of the hand is most consistent with acral myxoinflammatory fibroblastic sarcoma, a rare tumor known for its distinctive histological features and predilection for the acral regions.

rejected.label: Myxofibrosarcoma
rejected.why: Absence of typical curvilinear blood vessels and less inflammatory background

rejected.label: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor
rejected.why: Presence of lipoblast-like cells and Reed–Sternberg–like cells not typical for this entity

rejected.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
rejected.why: Unusual location and histological features not typical for a relapse of Hodgkin lymphoma
